change_summary: The PLOS ONE editors issued an Expression of Concern to inform readers of unresolved issues with the paper, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached. The notice reports an apparent vertical discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel between the 293T and A549 lanes. It also says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the Results statement that LSD1 siRNA reduced migration of H460 cells is not supported. The notice says the paper does not describe the controls for the Flag-LSD1 and LSD1 siRNA transfection experiments in enough detail to replicate them, while the abstract states that interrupting LSD1 with siRNA or pargyline suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion of A549, H460 and 293T cells. The notice also says similarities with work by other research groups call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, but it does not name the patient-tissue or survival analyses (Figs. 1–3, Table 1) among its specific issues.
evaluation: Section 2 of your draft cites Lv et al. for LSD1 being higher in lung cancer tissue than normal lung tissue in resected samples from 80 NSCLC patients, which the paper reports. It also says the controls for the transfection experiments are not described in enough detail to replicate them. The Section 3 use carries the most weight, because your draft says the main evidence behind its central hypothesis is a single cell-line study. The PLOS ONE editors issued an Expression of Concern to inform readers of unresolved issues, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached.
